records.reading_note: All five complete fields contain an omitted Prophetic body, a line-drawing topic pointer, Sufyan transmission criticism and compiler-appended legal explanations of line shape. Ahmad/IbnDawud quotations belong to that apparatus. Do not reconstruct the missing report or promote compiler explanation into the numbered report body.

IbnAbbas statement is explicitly raised by Shuba, while the later AbuDawud passage records a stopped-at-IbnAbbas alternative. Retain the source disagreement as context. The parenthetic passing-before-the-worshipper condition limits the supplied assertion and must remain. Preserve damaged Hindi wording, without a new attribution or spelling correction.

The first expressly quoted added utterance is finite despite the relative opening. A separate AbuMushir/Said version supplies the actual shorter utterance again; keep its report component distinct from the compiler introduction. Do not add the missing preceding incident.

AbuSahba reports IbnAbbas describing arrival with an unnamed boy, donkey, and two girls while the Prophet prayed and did not object. Full finite event with source-named participants; no identities are supplied for the unnamed children.

Fadl reports the Prophet praying in the open without a sutra while a donkey and female dog played. Open-place parentheses are lexical explanation; source narrative and actual lack of objection remain exact.

Wail prayer observations and Muhammad reporting HasanBasri response are distinct report components/speakers. The final AbuDawud omission comparison is context. The Urdu footnote reference is apparatus; do not turn Hasan speech or compiler criticism into Prophetic words.
Wail observed raised hands, thumb positions and takbir. The Hindi shoulder gloss is lexical context. Preserve source wording and its own sequence.

An explicitly abbreviated act places the right hand on the left, followed by a winter eyewitness detail. Keep the relative transmission and unnamed first-person witness qualified; do not invent the omitted preceding body or identify that witness from a neighboring occurrence.

Wail reports the companions raising their hands beneath clothes during a winter visit. Preserve the Companion-practice subject; the Prophet is the person visited, not an invented direct speaker or issuer of a command.

The first finite prostration detail is transmitted by Abbas from AbuHumayd, with its actor only relatively identified in these fields. The later IbnMubarak/Fulayh chain-memory discussion and similar-report pointer are apparatus. No missing actor name is supplied.

IbnMasud describes the earlier taught prayer act; Sad subsequently confirms it and reports the later knee-gripping instruction. Preserve both report stages and speakers. The supplied explanation of what the later command concerns must not be replaced by a guessed instruction.
Bara reports raising hands near the ears at prayer opening and not repeating the act. Both languages have a complete supplied report; no authenticity decision or cross-version harmonization is made.
Mughira reports noon prayer with the Prophet and the supplied instruction to delay until cooler. The explanation is part of the attributed statement; no modern advice is inferred.

AbuSaid describes delayed night prayer and the Prophet explanation about waiting, weaker people and illness. A chamber-origin parenthesis is explanatory context; preserve the complete source speech and its qualifying concern.
Aisha reports not sleeping before isha or talking without need afterward. The no-need parentheses restrict the assertion and must remain. The Urdu trailing footnote glyph is apparatus.

AbuMahdhura reports the taught adhan/iqama counts and formulas. All exact repetitions in Hindi remain. Urdu independently contains complete Arabic formulas and full supplied Urdu translations, all read to the end and retained as actual quoted/translated recitation. Only the final footnote marker is apparatus; do not shorten Urdu to the Hindi length.

AbuJuhayfa reports visiting the Prophet and witnessing Bilal call, turn and put fingers in his ears. The timing phrase quotes actual call words within the supplied report; do not turn these into an invented direct Prophetic instruction. Review lexical finger clarification separately from actual narrative details.
Uthman reports the final instruction concerning a muezzin taking wages. The Hindi money gloss is lexical context; preserve its damaged source spelling without harmonizing to Urdu.

Bilal reports the command to use the supplied taswib term in the dawn call and its prohibition in the night call. Do not expand that term from the next occurrence. Both Urdu footnote markers are apparatus.

Bilal supplies the repeated prayer-is-better-than-sleep formula and the subsequent retained dawn-call practice. The complete Hindi parenthetic translation is the translation of actual spoken words and remains, as does the Urdu supplied translation.

IbnUmar answers about gardens irrigated repeatedly after excrement use, and the source expressly attributes his report upward to the Prophet. Preserve that source attribution and his own framing; do not claim the entire framing is a direct Prophetic quotation.
IbnUmar transmits the seven-place prayer prohibition with the exact source list. Slaughterhouse explanatory parentheses are context; do not alter the seven listed sites.
Hindi, Urdu and Roman Urdu are explicit unavailable-report placeholders; Arabic and English are actually empty. All nonempty siblings were fully read. No body or translation is invented.
The source names Anas and reports the lost knowledge of LaylatQadr, followed by the exact unusual night sequence21,23,25,29,27. Do not reorder numbers or replace its narrator from another edition.
The source names AbdullahibnDinar and reports clothing prohibitions plus the cut-below-ankle fallback. Do not insert a missing IbnUmar link. The Hindi sandal gloss is lexical context.

Aisha reports perfuming before entering ihram and before the visitation circumambulation on leaving it. Preserve each language own wording about ihram, without silently translating the object differently.

Salim reports IbnUmar correcting a claim about the unnamed plain and describing talbiya by the DhulHulayfa mosque. Keep this as IbnUmar criticism with its attributed practice; do not supply a name for the plain.

Aisha reports the farewell-pilgrimage group, three entry types, the source own hajj-only statement about the Prophet and the differing exit times. Preserve the source version without reconciling it to other versions.

Sila describes a meal and Ammar saying a person fasting on the doubtful day disobeyed AbuQasim. Ammar is the actual speaker. Subsequent grading, other-report references and legal practice are compiler context; the Urdu footnote glyph is apparatus.

Anas reports a one-month ila, a 29-day stay and subsequent dialogue. The ila definition is lexical context. The parenthetic return to the wives is supplied narrative action, and the also qualifier preserves the can-be-29 scope. Compiler grading is separate.
All five complete fields are chain/similar-to-700 pointers and grading, without an actual report body. The English narrator name does not supply a missing matn. Preserve as source-only.

AbuAtiyya and Masruq ask Aisha about two companions; she confirms the Prophet followed the early breaking/prayer practice. Keep the complete dialogue and own source names. Urdu footnote references and later grading/name-variant explanation are context.

The source explicitly quotes the abbreviated quantity phrase for reciting fifty verses. It is actual supplied wording, not a bare pointer. Do not invent its omitted question, event or interval. Subsequent grading, other-source pointer and juristic application are context.
AbuSaid explicitly reports the Prophet not objecting to either fasting or not fasting during Ramadan travel. Keep that attribution separate from the compiler grade.

AbuSaid describes companions traveling with the Prophet, their mutual lack of criticism, and their own judgment about strength/weakness. These are the companions practice and assessment, not newly manufactured direct Prophetic speech.
UmmHani supplies a complete drinking/voluntary-fast dialogue with the Prophet. The following compiler reference to other reports is context, without importing any of those reports.
Aisha reports the question about something to eat, her negative answer and the Prophet saying he is fasting. Do not add a later meal or any unprinted continuation.

Aisha/Hafsa meal and make-up-fast dialogue is a complete numbered report. The father-daughter aside belongs to Aisha narrative. The subsequent long isnad-criticism conversation and legal opinions are compiler apparatus, not further numbered events.

Hindi stops within the quoted descent-to-the-lower-sky statement before damaged compiler text; Urdu independently supplies the further forgiveness clause. Preserve the language mismatch, source spelling, and own truncation. Do not fill Hindi from Urdu; the Urdu footnote reference and final grading/transmission discussion are context.

IbnUmar reports nonfasting at Arafat with the Prophet and three named caliphs, then states his own practice without commanding or forbidding. Keep location/scope and all actual speakers distinct; the following chain/name discussion is context.

scope: Actual second complete reading of all40 Hindi/Urdu pairs and all nonempty siblings of AbuDawud690, Tirmidhi701 and Malik684; not an automatic admission ledger.
